issues.description: The problem statement (text and UML) indicates that Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a boolean (text: "should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise" and UML: messageOnMilk():boolean), but the solution implements Milkable.messageOnMilk() with return type String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) and Goat/Seal return String messages. This mismatch will confuse students about the expected return type and will cause tests or example code to disagree with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and implementation. Either (A) change the problem statement and UML to require messageOnMilk() to return String (and update the textual description to show example return strings), which matches the solution, or (B) change the solution and its Milkable interface to return boolean and update Goat/Seal implementations and any tests to return true/false accordingly. Preferably update the problem statement to specify String if the intended examples are textual messages.

issues.description: There is an internal contradiction within the problem statement UML: the Seal class UML lists messageOnMilk():String while the Milkable interface UML (and a textual description) specify messageOnMilk():boolean. This inconsistency inside the specification will confuse students about the correct signature to implement for classes that implement Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the internal contradiction in the problem statement: make the UML for Seal and the Milkable interface show the same return type for messageOnMilk(). Update the textual description to match that chosen type. Prefer making both UML entries and the text use the same type (String if textual milking messages are intended, or boolean if only success/failure is intended).

issues.description: The method messageOnMilk() is inconsistently specified across artifacts: the UML and textual instructions in the problem statement describe/expect a boolean return (indicating success of milking), while the Seal/Goat class diagrams and the solution implementation define messageOnMilk() to return a String (e.g., "Seal <name> is milked"). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected interface signature and lead to incompatible implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification for messageOnMilk() across all artifacts. Prefer updating the problem statement (UML and textual instructions) to state that messageOnMilk() returns a String (a descriptive message, e.g., "<AnimalType> <name> is milked") to match the solution, or conversely change the solution to return boolean and update associated examples. Ensure the Milkable interface, class diagrams, and textual task description all use the same signature.
